original_value: Both entity and relation extraction can benefit from being performed jointly, allowing each task to correct the errors of the other. Most existing neural joint methods extract entities and relations separately and achieve joint learning  through parameter sharing, leading to a drawback that information between output entities and relations cannot be fully exploited. In this paper, we convert the joint task into a directed graph by designing a novel graph scheme and propose a transition-based approach to generate the directed graph incrementally, which can achieve joint learning through joint decoding. Our method can model underlying dependencies not only between entities and relations, but also between relations. Experiments on NewYork Times (NYT) corpora show that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

result.paraphrase: Jointly performing entity and relation extraction can improve both tasks by letting them fix one another’s mistakes. Most current neural joint methods still extract entities and relations separately, using parameter sharing for joint learning and thus failing to fully exploit information among the predicted entities and relations. In this paper, we redesign the joint task as a directed graph with a new graph scheme and introduce a transition-based method that incrementally constructs the directed graph, enabling joint learning through joint decoding. Our approach can capture latent dependencies not only between entities and relations, but also among relations themselves. Experiments on the NewYork Times (NYT) corpora demonstrate that it surpasses state-of-the-art methods.
